chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, who said:

Regarding a man who had several slaves, he said, 'Whichever of you teaches me a Verse from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, he is free.' One of them taught him. Then the master died, and it was not known which of them was the one who taught him the Verse. 'Can a lot be drawn?' He said: 'Yes, and it is not allowed for anyone to extract him except for the Imam, for he has a specific speech at the time of drawing the lot which he recites, and a supplication which no one knows besides him, nor is anyone able over it apart from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the role of the Imam in drawing lots to free a slave when the master's identity of the teacher is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the procedure for emancipating a slave when the master dies without specifying which slave taught him a Quranic verse, establishing that the Imam alone has the authority to draw lots (qur'ah) to identify the specific slave. The Imam utilizes a unique recitation and supplication known only to him, highlighting the concept of 'kalam' (speech) specific to the Imam's role in legal adjudication. This ruling underscores the Imam's exclusive jurisdiction in resolving ambiguities regarding manumission conditions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who had a number of owned slaves. So he said, ‘Whichever of you teaches me a Verse from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, so he is free’. So one of them taught him. Then the master died, and it was not known which of them was the one who taught him the Verse. Can a lot be drawn?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and it is not allowed for anyone to extract him except for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, as for it is speech (to be recited), and a time for the drawing of lots, and a supplication which no one knows besides him<sup>asws</sup>, nor is anyone able over it apart from him<sup>asws</sup>’.
